en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on the Maidenhood:
81. The Training Rule for Those Undergoing Probation.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, at the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, thinking,
“I will give full admission to a trainee nun,” assembled the elder bhikkhus; but seeing an abundance of fresh and cooked food,
she said, “Venerable sirs, I will not give full admission to the trainee nun for the time being,” and having dismissed the elder bhikkhus, [she went to] Devadatta.
Having assembled Kokālika, Kaṭamodakatissaka, Samuddadatta—the son of Khaṇḍadevī—and others, she gave the full admission to a trainee nun (sikkhamānā).
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before] ...were indignant, complained, and grumbled:
"How can the noble lady Thullanandā give the full admission to a trainee nun by means of the granting of consent from those on probation?"... [as before] ...
“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā ordains a trainee nun by means of giving consent while she herself is on probation?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordain a *sikkhamānā* by means of giving consent while she herself is on probation?
This, monks, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: [The full rule follows]"

“Whatever nun, however, should give the higher ordination to a trainee (sikkhamānā) by means of the granting of consent while she herself is on probation, that is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [etc.]
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"By giving consent while on probation" means:
When the assembly has risen.
A trainee nun (sikkhamānā) is one who has trained for two years in the six rules.
"Should give the full admission" means:
she should confer the higher ordination (*upasampadā*).
If, thinking "I will give the full admission," she searches for a group, a preceptor (*ācariyā*), a bowl, or a robe, or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For two proclamations, there are offenses of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the proclamation, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for the preceptor.
There is an offense of wrong-doing for the group and for the preceptor.
There is no offense if she ordains her when the assembly has not yet risen.
"Of one who is insane,
of one who is a first-offender.
The eleventh training rule is finished.
